Best-value Seoul hotels for first-time visitors

Where to stay in Seoul: Myeongdong vs Hongdae vs Gangnam vs Jongno
facts: Myeongdong: central, shopping, many hotels, easy airport bus and subway
Hongdae: young crowd, cafes, nightlife, direct airport rail (AREX) link
Gangnam: business district, upscale shopping, nightlife, further from old palaces
Jongno/Bukchon: palaces, hanok, traditional streets, quieter at night

topics.title_hint: Seoul transport: T-money card and subway tips for visitors
facts: T-money is a rechargeable transit card for subway and buses; usable at convenience stores
Seoul subway lines are color coded with English signs and announcements
Airport Railroad (AREX) connects Incheon Airport to Seoul Station and Hongdae

topics.title_hint: Stay connected in Korea: eSIM and pocket Wi-Fi for tourists
facts: Travelers commonly use an eSIM, a local SIM, or pocket Wi-Fi
Free Wi-Fi is common in cafes, subway stations and many public places
Set up an eSIM before arrival if your phone supports it

topics.title_hint: Incheon Airport to Seoul: train, bus or taxi
facts: AREX airport railroad runs to Seoul Station and Hongdae
Airport limousine buses serve many major hotels
Taxis and pre-booked transfers are an option with heavy luggage

topics.title_hint: Tax refund and K-beauty shopping tips in Seoul
facts: Tourists can often claim a tax refund on qualifying purchases at participating shops
Olive Young and similar stores are popular for K-beauty
Palaces and Bukchon Hanok Village are in central Seoul
DMZ tours depart from Seoul and require advance booking with a passport
Nami Island and Suwon Hwaseong Fortress are popular half or full day trips
